title: pricing-packaging-scratchpad-olivia
content:
Quick back-of-envelope notes for pricing / packaging. Mostly thinking out loud — rough numbers, assumptions listed. Not final.

Context / goal:
- Want simple hosted pricing that covers unit costs + decent margin, while having clear upgrade path to Dedicated and Private.
- Keep free/dev onboarding friction low (small free token bucket). Create predictable paid tiers for startups and enterprise with reserved capacity options.

Assumptions (rough):
- Baseline marginal cost (compute + infra + networking + amortized infra ops) for typical generation model ~ $4 per 1M tokens (prompt + completion). This is our internal run-time cost for optimized quantized variants on pooled infra.
- Heavier models (longer context / more compute) -> up to 3x cost (so ~$12 / 1M).
- Embeddings: ~ $2 per 1M embed calls (simple small model), or $0.000002 per vector (if 1 vector per call).
- Request overhead (api, egress, storage) baked into above.
- Payment / billing, support, and card fees ~ 5% on top of revenue; sales/discounts handled separately.

Channel pricing benchmark (target):
- Break-even price per 1M tokens = $4 (cost).
- Target gross margin (hosted) = 60% -> list price ~= $10 per 1M tokens.
- Startup discount / committed rate (Dedicated) = $6 per 1M tokens (requires monthly commit).
- Enterprise / Private: license + ops, negotiate (base platform fee + low per-token rate, e.g., $2-$4 /1M for dedicated/on-prem).

Example usage scenarios (for sanity checks):
1) Simple chat app (avg tokens per user per day = 1k (prompt+resp), 2 messages/day)
   - MAU = 100k -> monthly tokens = 100k * 2 * 30 * 1000 = 6B tokens/month
   - Our cost @ $4 / 1M = 6k * $4 = $24,000 / month
   - Revenue @ $10 / 1M = 6k * $10 = $60,000 / month -> gross margin = $36k (60%)

2) Higher-quality assistant (avg tokens 3k per user/day)
   - Same MAU -> tokens = 18B -> cost = 18k * $4 = $72k, revenue = $180k -> margin $108k

3) Embeddings-heavy app (search + retrieval)
   - 10M embed calls/month @ $2 / 1M (~$0.000002 per vector) -> cost = 10 * $2 = $20
   - This seems suspiciously low (we need to validate embed model cost). Re-check: if each embed call costs $0.0004 (more realistic) then 10M * 0.0004 = $4k. OK need concrete benching.

Tier ideas (hosted API):
- Free: 100k tokens / month + 1k embed calls. (Onboarding, limited throughput, no SLAs)
- Developer: $20 / month -> 2M tokens + 10k embeds, community support, rate-limited to maintain fairness
- Startup: $500 / month -> 100M tokens + 100k embeds, email support, 2 concurrent requests, up to N requests/s burst
- Scale: $3k / month -> 1B tokens + 1M embeds, higher concurrency, analytics, model pinning
- Enterprise: custom pricing, reserved capacity options, SLA/uptime/backups / audit logs. Commit discount to $6 / 1M tokens for committed volumes.

Dedicated / Reserved model ideas:
- Offer committed-perf buckets: e.g., commit $X/month for baseline throughput (guaranteed GPU pool) + burst to hosted at pay-as-you-go price.
- Example: 50% discount vs hosted price with 6-12 month commit -> $6 / 1M tokens (vs $10). 
- Also offer concurrency-based pricing (reserved vCPU/GPU hours) for predictability.

Private / On-prem:
- License fee + monthly ops fee + per-token reporting if we run any managed components. Typically negotiated. Base assumptions: on-prem customers care about isolation more than unit price.

Unit economics checklist (what to validate):
- Real marginal cost per 1M tokens by model family (quantized 8-bit vs FP16 vs huge transformer). Instrument metrics per model + per-seq-length distribution. (PRIORITY)
- Embed cost per call for our small/medium embed models. Current bench inconsistent; need a microbench run.
- Effective utilization/packing: how much do batching and KV cache reduce per-token cost in typical workloads? Add caching uplift factor (e.g., 10-40% savings).
- Outlier cost: long-context sessions (50k tokens) — define surcharge or cap.
- Billing accuracy: round to nearest 1k tokens, minimum charge thresholds?

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we charge prompt+completion together or only output tokens? Industry varies; charging both is straightforward and aligns incentives for shorter prompts.
- Free tier size — 100k tokens seems OK, but might be too generous for vector-heavy starter apps. Consider separate embed quota.
- Do we want feature gating by tier (e.g., model family access, streaming, function-calls)? Probably yes.
- SLA / overage model for Dedicated: when they burst above commit, charge committed rate + overage at hosted price? Define max burst.

Quick pricing sensitivity table (hosted):
- If price = $8 / 1M -> margin = (8-4)/8 = 50%
- If price = $10 / 1M -> margin 60%
- If price = $12 / 1M -> margin 66%
Aim: keep hosted price between $8-$12 / 1M; default $10 for public docs.

Billing UX notes:
- Show token计数 in console per route/model, projected monthly spend with current usage patterns.
- Provide cost alerts at usage thresholds (50%, 80%, 100%).
- Allow customers to lock model family to cheaper quantized variant for cost control.

Notes to self / action items:
- Run cost microbench for: base (v1-small), medium (v1-medium), large (v1-large, fp16), quantized-8bit for 1M token throughput numbers. Record $/1M tokens per model. (owner: Riley)
- Decide default public price + developer tier bundles (owner: me)
- Draft a short one-pager showing examples for startups (MAU 10k/100k/1M) and cost sensitivity.

Links / refs:
- CONFLUENCE-PRICING-OVERVIEW (placeholder)
- JIRA-PRIC-123 (ticket for microbench)

Rough brain dump ends here. Clean up and formalize after we have microbench numbers.

-- Olivia
